entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 3_Juno_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 13506 vertices and 27008 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Size and pole
entries.finding: The retained Table 1 and Table A.1 extract records diameter 254 km, ecliptic J2000 pole (105°, 18°), period 7.209531 h. Published survey diameter averages ADAM and MPCD; the released MPCD coordinates are not rescaled to that average. The measured source volume-equivalent radius is 126.11549995574961 km. These source interpretations were checked against the recipe; the paper table was not freshly re-transcribed in this pass.

entries.subject: Released SPHERE observations and surface registration
entries.finding: The live source folder https://observations.lam.fr/astero/Data/3Juno/ contains Deconv/ and Red/. Reduced and deconvolved observations therefore have a concrete archive route. Their pixels, image geometry, coverage and photometry were not qualified in this directory-level check, so these files cannot yet be treated as a registered global reflectance map. The current grid remains an explicit missing-imagery presentation.
entries.revisitWhen: The original image headers and publication establish a usable projection onto this specific MPCD model, and a native-pixel comparison qualifies geometry, illumination and measured coverage.

entries.subject: Released ADAM companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 3_Juno_adam.obj. The body’s retained model comparison already distinguishes this ADAM reconstruction from the selected MPCD mesh. It is not adopted as a duplicate view of the same measured shape; the original comparison remains linked.
entries.revisitWhen: An observation or scientific comparison specifically requires this alternative mesh and its matching source frame.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 30 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 4999 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.07 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.36; 0 of 30 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. A photograph lens for this body would rest on the survey's record read by the route proven on Vesta and on five elongated bodies, with no check on this body itself; it is not derived until one exists. Corrected on the silhouette: the outline does judge this body, though only in part. Of 30 frames, 5 project an outline elongated enough to define a position angle and they leave 2.485 degrees after a 2.151-degree floor, inside the three-degree gate, while the other 25 are round. A lens on five scoring frames is thin but is not the same as having no check at all, so this is a live candidate rather than a closed no-go. Measured outside preparation by the registration stage's own limb rule driven from the pinned inputs, which reproduces Sylvia's prepared report to the digit; the stage's own number can differ, and on Themis it read 1.65 degrees where this route read 2.92.
entries.revisitWhen: Preparation of the lens, to have the stage judge those five scoring frames itself, or a registration reference independent of the outline.
